name: text-flipping-board
title: Split Flap Board
description: Recreates a mechanical split-flap display as a grid of tiles. Each character flips through random letters before landing on its target, with a few tiles filled in solid colour as accents.
use: A hero or event page wants a nostalgic mechanical board that cycles through messages.
avoid: It is locked to a 22 by 6 character grid, so longer copy is clipped, and every change replays the whole flip.
a11y: The board has no aria-live or label, so assistive tech gets a stream of changing single characters. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark rounded panel holds a grid of small square tiles, most near-black with a faint horizontal split line. A few tiles glow solid red, orange, yellow, green, blue or violet, and pale monospace characters sit on the others.
behaves: Each character tile cycles through random letters, then flips over to its target with delays spreading across rows and columns. The message settles among coloured accent tiles and holds until the text changes again.
customise: Supply text or row strings, use {R}-style codes for colour tiles, and set a duration; the grid size and palette are fixed in the source.
weight: moderate: Up to 132 tiles each flip through dozens of characters with timers and 3D transforms.
